News.title: I decided to marry MYSELF – it’s led to horrendous dates, constant ‘affairs’ & trolls calling me a ‘man-hating spinster’
News.content:
SOPHIE Tanner walked down the aisle linking arms with her proud dad – but there was no one waiting for her at the altar.

Instead, the blushing bride read out a singular version of traditional wedding vows – promising to love herself “til death do we part”.



Sophie, 47, had endured a string of bad relationships – the latest of which saw her boyfriend cheat with a mutual friend, before she made a big step and tied the knot to the only true “constant” in her life.



Following the messiest of break-ups, she’d begun writing a novel, which would eventually be published as Reader, I Married Me.

During her research, she learned about sologamy, the act of marrying oneself in a symbolic ceremony to affirm self-love.

And so, in a case of art imitating life, she followed in the footsteps of her main character Chloe Usher and said “I do” in her home town of Brighton in 2015, making headlines around the world.

Dressed in a £100 secondhand wedding dress, she moved through the square with her bridesmaids and wedding guests, encouraging passersby to join the flashmob to the church.

There, one of her pals dressed as the Pope “ordained” the union before she invited all attendees to join her in her first dance.



Then there was a beach party reception and later a solo trip to Uganda to go gorilla trekking in place of a honeymoon.

She even renewed her vows to herself a few years later in 2019.



Sophie told The Sun: “After a few bad relationships and being cheated on, I wanted to work on my relationship with myself and my self-worth, and give myself a bit of a boost.”

She said the concept came to her in a “brainwave”, explaining: “I was writing a book about the same thing and I was coming to the end of it.

“I thought I love it and I do want to do this myself.”

At the time, Sophie was volunteering at Brighton Fringe Festival and came across a stage on the steps of the town’s Unitarian Church which “would be perfect” for the ceremony, which was hastily arranged.



“I thought I’ll have it as like a wedding event, and use the tropes of a wedding and open it up, and it flowed quite nicely with people passing by and joining in,” she said.

She was joined by family and friends, with it taking on the vibe of a “pop up street event”.

“We made an aisle, and me and my bridesmaids danced through the streets in almost like a flashmob,” she explained.

“My dad was there and walked me up to my friend who was dressed up like the Pope.”



Sophie was going to write her own vows but decided on adapting the traditional wedding ones to the singular.

“They’re about facing disappointments and embracing your dreams, and being your own best friend,” she said.

“Switching them up to singular made them more powerful.”

Sophie admitted to even pre-wedding nerves the night before.



“I did feel jittery,” she said. “It was more, ‘am I really doing this?’ It was quite a public spectacle.

“It was so random and left field.”

As part of her research, she asked her local ceremonies office if she could make the union official with all the usual formalities, but says they refused.

Sophie said: “Then I thought a lot of the legalities around marriage, when it’s two people, are about protecting your assets.

“Because it’s just me, my assets are my own anyway. I just thought I’ll have the ceremony without the formality.”



She was inspired by “coming of age rituals” often associated with ancient tribes around the world.

“Some tribes do things like jumping over cows and celebrate someone’s path into adulthood,” she said.

“They’re nothing to do with marriage, it’s just the fact they’re coming of age.



“There’s no real ritual for becoming an adult in the West, and you don’t feel properly grown up until you’re married.”

She added: “It felt to me like a ritual thing. Having everyone be there and witness me doing vows, it felt like a nice ritual.”

However, with news of her self-wedding spreading around the world, over the last 11 years Sophie has experienced all kinds of reactions, including a harsh brigade of online critics.



“It was only when it was in the newspapers and stuff I started realising I got backlash and got trolls,” she said.

“I got invited to radio shows in America and they were horrible to me.”

Sophie accepts she may have become seen by some as a “hardcore spinster rejecting men forever, with cobwebs all over her”, similar to Charles Dickens’ famous jilted bride Miss Havisham.

But that was never the case, and she has been “cheating” on herself with other men, going on dates for years despite her marital status.

“Some guys I’ve dated have reacted in different ways,” she said laughing and admits she is even open to marrying someone else one day.



“My self wedding was about self love, a wedding to another person is about romantic love,” she said.

“I’ll always keep that relationship for myself, regardless of whatever relationship I get into.

“But if I want to celebrate that relationship with a wedding, why not?”

In fact, telling potential partners that she’s already married to herself has proved to be a good gauge for finding the right life partner.



She said: “I have to explain it’s not that I’m anti-men or anti couples.

“I was surprised, one guy said ‘you can’t have your cake and eat it’ and got angry.

“In a way, it was a good way of filtering people out early.

“If they react strongly, I know they’re not the guy for me. Others were really intrigued and would read my book, and it’d say more about them.”



In recent months, she even began a relationship with Dom, a single dad of teenagers.

“Since my self-wedding, I hadn’t got into a relationship where we were girlfriend and boyfriend until Dom really,” she explained.

“I was a bit hyper independent. Maybe I needed to be a bit more open.”

She said that relationship was the best romantic coupling she’d ever had.



“Sometimes you make bad decisions with the wrong people, but knowing what I didn’t want, I just felt the relationship with him was right at the time,” she said.

They separated earlier this year but there’s no hard feelings from Sophie.



She said, ultimately, relationships with others can be varying, with many marriages ending in divorce.

“You can outgrow each other, you’re different people in your 20s, for example,” she explained.

“That’s why for me marrying myself is the only constant, because it’s until death do we part.

“My relationship with myself is always going to be the most important because others come and go.

“Marrying myself was all about making sure I always check in with me.



“Anyone else who can compliment my journey along the way is great.”

News.title: Who is Jack Brooksbank, Princess Eugenie’s husband?
News.content:
JACK THE LAD Who is Jack Brooksbank, Princess Eugenie’s husband?

PRINCESS Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank have been married since 2018.

The couple has had one of the most low-profile romances within the Royal Family, but who is Jack Brooksbank? Read on to find out.

Who is Jack Brooksbank?

Jack Brooksbank was born on May 3, 1986, in London, England, and is the oldest son of George and Nicola Brooksbank.

He has a younger brother named Thomas, who works in business management for a London-based asset management firm.

Jack went to private Stowe school in Buckinghamshire and then to the University of Bristol but left without finishing to start working.

He worked at the Admiral Codrington pub in Chelsea before going on to the Markham Inn where he spent three formative years.

He has spoken fondly of how much he learned from the “strange” and “demanding” Sloane ranger clientele.

It is believed that he met Prince Harry and club baron Guy Pelly at the bar he was working in, who hired him to manage the world-famous, exclusive night spot Mahiki, in Mayfair.

Jack left in 2010 to start his own wine merchant and was a brand manager of Casamigos Tequila, co-founded by George Clooney before the brand was sold.

What is his net worth?

Jack’s net worth has not been disclosed to the public.

However, as a former brand ambassador of Casamigos tequila, an impressive background in luxury hospitality and a wine merchant, it is safe to say the royal has quite the stash of cash in the bank

Clooney sold Casamigos tequila to Diageo for a staggering $1billion (£700million) in 2020, so Jack no doubt earned a hefty sum from that too.

In 2022, he began working in marketing and sales for property developer Michael Meldman’s Discovery Land company in Portugal.

His new role sees him split his time between the UK and Portugal.

How did Jack meet Eugenie?

The pair first met on the Swiss ski slopes of Verbier where Princess Eugenie had gone to celebrate her father, Prince Andrew’s 50th birthday.

Eugenie was just 19 at the time, in February 2010, and studying English, politics and history at Newcastle University.

The Princess and Jack got on extremely well and a connection was formed that endured a period of long-distance while she worked in New York in 2013.

The pair are said to have chatted over Skype to keep the fire burning despite being kept apart by thousands of miles and several hours worth of time zone.

When did he and Princess Eugenie announce their engagement?

Buckingham Palace released a statement on January 22, 2018, announcing that the young couple were engaged and would wed in the autumn of 2018.

They got engaged while on holiday in Nicaragua in January 2018.

Buckingham Palace said: “The Duke and Duchess of York are delighted to announce the engagement of Princess Eugenie to Mr Jack Brooksbank.

“Her Royal Highness and Mr Brooksbank became engaged in Nicaragua earlier this month.

“The wedding will take place in the autumn of 2018 at St George’s Chapel in Windsor, with further details to be announced in due course.”

When did he marry Eugenie?

Jack married Princess Eugenie on October 12, 2018, in Windsor.

They wed at the same venue as Prince Harry’s wedding to Meghan Markle.

His brother Tom was the best man.

Do they have any children?

They had their first child, named August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, on February 9, 2021, at the Portland Hospital in London.

He was born by caesarean section due to her childhood scoliosis operation.

Their second child, Ernest Brooksbank, was born on May 30, 2023 at the same hospital.

More recently, the couple have announced they are expecting a third child this year.

Eugenie, who usually keeps a low profile on social media, posted a picture to her Instagram of her children holding an ultrasound captioned with: “Baby Brooksbank due 2026!”

The couple announced in January 2023 that they were expecting a second child.

Their second son, Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, was born on May 30, 2023.

News.title: Dramatic moment cop is lowered into crocodile-infested river to retrieve hotel boss still INSIDE beast
News.content:
THIS is the incredible moment a police diver was lowered into a crocodile-infested river to retrieve the body of a missing hotel boss.

Gabriel Batista, 59, was swept away in raging floodwaters and cops now suspect he was eaten by a ravenous killer croc in the swampy waters of South Africa.





Police spent four days flying a drone over the man-eating croc before shooting it dead and airlifting it off the predator-riddled island to check out their hunch.

Incredible footage showed a brave police commander hauled hundreds of feet up into the air to retrieve the carcass.

When the half-ton carnivore was lowered down to the ground in the nearby Kruger National Park its belly was sliced open to see if the huge beast did indeed eat the missing businessman.

The field necropsy carried out by South African Police Captain Joey Potgieter led to the macabre discovery of two severed arms with hands still attached, half a rib cage and chest flesh.



A ring believed to belong to missing businessman Gabriel Batista, 59, was also said to have been found on one of the fingers.

DNA checks to confirm the corpse’s identity are now being carried out.

However, in a sickening twist, police investigating the incident at the town of Komatipoort in Mpumalanga Province found a further six pairs of shoes inside the crocodile’s stomach.

None of the shoes belonged to victim Gabriel Batista leading to fears that the crocodile was a rogue maneater that had killed or eaten many drowning victims in the river over recent years.



Crocodiles cannot digest plastic according to wildlife experts hence the remains of the shoes including flip flops, sandals, Nike trainers and high heels being found inside its body.

A full investigation has been launched to try and link the shoes to missing local residents or villagers who use the often flooded bridge and had been swept away.

The horror accident unfolded last Monday when businessman Batista tried to drive over a flooded low level bridge to reach his hotel and bar on the other side.



But the vicious currents pushed his 4×4 Ford Ranger over the side and onto rocks and the businessman is believed to have climbed out of the vehicle to try and wade to safety.

But police suspect the strength of the water washed him off his feet and down the Komati River towards the nearby border with Mozambique and the hungry crocodiles.

Police and wildlife rangers said dozens of the fearsome carnivores use the muddy islands in the river and the sandy banks to lie in wait for prey swept downstream.

It is not known if Batista drowned before being eaten by the crocodile.

It is therefore possible that his remains are also inside several other roaming crocs.



The victim owned the Border Country Inn and sports bar just a short drive from the regularly flooded bridge and 3 miles from the world-famous Kruger National Park.

A spokesman said: “Gabriel was a lovely guy and a family man who was married with lots of kids and he spent a lot of time up here and customers loved him.

“He lived in Johannesburg but owned this guest house and bar and spent a lot of time here and was on his way to work on Monday when he was just swept away.



“The famiy do not want to say anything until the DNA results have been done. It is just terrible and his wife has been here every day with the police diving team.

“It is a nightmare but at the moment there is no family comment” she said.

The bravery of the police dive team commander Captain Johan “Pottie” Potgieter has been hailed after he volunteered to be airlifted in to retrieve the shot-dead croc.

His team suspected that Batista had been eaten and sent up a drone on Tuesday and monitored the activity of the resident crocodiles on the mudbank islands.

Captain Potgieter said: “My dive team have been recovering bodies from local rivers in this part of South Africa for a long time so we know the behaviour or crocodiles.



“From a drone we studied a number of crocodiles on an island 60m from the bridge and we identified one particular croc we were 100% certain had eaten the man.

“This very large one was not moving in the sun and showed typical signs of recent feeding as it has a massively full tummy and stayed out of the nearby water.

“He made no effort to move despite the noise of the drones or our chopper overhead or any inclination to seek out food so we were sure it was this crocodile” he said.



Permission had to be sought to euthanise the crocodile which was given on Saturday and he was killed with a single shot from a marksman on the police helicopter.

The next task was to recover the predator from the crocodile infested island.

Captain Potgieter said: “I got the job and was put into a harness and the noise of the gunshot and the helicopter that lowered me down scattered the other crocodiles.

“There was so many things that could go wrong and the rope basically lowered me onto the snout of the crocodile so I was kind of hoping it really was properly dead!

“There were two crocs nearby watching as I slipped the harness around the waist of the dead crocodile and secured it under the front legs and tightened the strap.



“Then I signalled to the chopper and it just took me straight up leaving a lot of big crocodiles behind and then we flew to a landing zone to open the croc up” he said.

His police service wife Captain Joey Potgieter opened up the dead crocodile.

Captain Johan Potgieter said: “I don’t want to go into too much detail but there was enough inside the stomach to lead us to believe the crocodile ate the missing man.



“But we will have to wait until the DNA results come back to confirm it” he said.

Lieut General Puleng Dimpane, acting National Police Commissioner, commended the extraordinary bravery and selflessness displayed by Captain Potgieter.

She said: “His willingness to place his own life in danger is going far beyond the call of duty to try and bring some form of closure to the family and shows great bravery.

“It reflects the unwavering commitment of South African Police members to do the right thing even in the face of a danger that could have cost him his very life”.

The Nile crocodile is amongst Africa’s most feared predators and has one of the strongest bites in the animal kingdom which has 8 times of the force of the Great White Shark.



They kill 1000 people a year in Africa and grow up to 20ft long and weight up to 1500lbs and can run at 22mph and are no match for a human and few are lucky to escape their attack.

They feed mainly on fish but can easily take down buffalo, antelope, young hippo and young elephants and have 64 to 68 teeth up to five inches long to grip and hold onto their prey.

Busi Chafuza said on Facebook: “Killing the crocodile is not going to bring this man back but the family will be able to bury their loved one with dignity and will have a grave for him”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Deep McCent said: “Sadly the crocodile had to die as once it was considered a man-eater it becomes very dangerous because it loses their fear of humans and sees them as prey”.

Sikes Mosime said: “We all die different but imagine trying to swim to safety after your car gets swept away by water and all of a sudden a big lizard pounces and that is the end”.

News.title: Putin has fragile control & tyrant’s regime will snap, ex-CIA boss warns… UK and US ‘must be prepared for bloodshed’
News.content:
TYRANT TIPPING POINT Putin has fragile control & tyrant’s regime will snap, ex-CIA boss warns… UK and US ‘must be prepared for bloodshed’

VLADIMIR Putin’s regime is ready to “snap” at any moment and spark a violent crisis, an ex-CIA boss has warned.

The UK and US must be prepared for bloodshed as Putin’s popularity rapidly diminishes in Russia, former senior agent Glenn Corn said.





The tyrant’s war in Ukraine has weakened his control as he faces mounting losses on the battlefield and economic collapse at home.

And as signs of a looming regime collapse emerge, experts warn the outcome will result in “chaos”.

Former senior CIA executive Glenn Corn told The Sun: “The US and Europe need to be prepared for such an event.”

Some 1.2million Russian soldiers have been killed, wounded or are missing since Putin ordered his invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

The war has tanked Russia’s economy, forcing defence costs up to 15.5trillion roubles (£144bn) in 2025, while food prices spiked by 18.6 per cent in just two years.

Now even hard-line Kremlin supporters are breaking rank to turn against their out-of-touch dictator.

But if Putin’s regime falls apart, experts say Russia’s aggression towards the West will continue.

Anothny Glees, Director of European Studies at Brunel University, told The Sun: “Putin has corrupted Russia. His successors, whether political or military, will carry on with his policy.



“We should expect ongoing fighting in Ukraine but also moves against NATO.

“Either on its Eastern Flank – which puts the UK in the firing line – or from the Arctic.”

The dictator has restructured the state, economy, and even the school system around his war in Ukraine.



Senior Lecturer Dr Ruth Deyermond at the Department of War Studies at King’s College said: “The UK must recognise that Putin sees his invasion as a ‘war against the West’.

“And among Western states, Britain is the number one target of Russian government hatred.”

In the face of Russia’s brazen aggression, the UK must urgently build up its defence capabilities, analysts say.

“The UK needs to spend more on defence, and do it more efficiently,” Dr Deyermond added.

“For decades, far too much money has been wasted in the defence procurement process; the UK can’t afford to keep doing that.”



For now, the West must control Putin – who may use “the threat of an invasion” to “keep Europe off balance”, ex-CIA chief Corn said.

He doubts the Kremlin tsar’s ability to launch an attack, but warned Britain must repair its relationship with the US if it hopes to defeat the dictator.

The alliance between the UK and US is at a 70-year low after Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer refused to support Donald Trump’s war in Iran.



Corn said: “It leaves the impression that Europeans want the US to serve their interests but when called upon for assistance by Washington, will not respond.”

Europe’s “short-sighted” response will open a door for Moscow to exploit America’s sense of betrayal, Corn said.

And Russia continues to benefit from emerging divides in the West.

Moscow is waging information warfare on its enemies to disrupt threats to Putin’s control.

Corn said: “Russia is using social media and disinformation tactics to fuel conspiracy theories, keeping its opponents fighting amongst themselves and distracted from Moscow’s own internal weaknesses.”



Meanwhile, US dominance throughout the war with Iran will be a wake up call for the Russian Security Establishment.

The US has hit Iran with weeks of relentless blitzes, depleting its resources and killing many of its most powerful players.

Corn added: “Russian military technology has been shown to be less than effective and not competitive on the battlefield with US and Israeli technology.

“The US controls the skies over Iran from across the Atlantic while Moscow cannot control their skies in Ukraine, a country that sits on Russia’s border.



“In fact, Moscow cannot protect its own skies from repeated Ukrainian air attacks that have hit targets deep inside of Russia on many occasions.

“This reality is humiliating to many Russians, including in the security establishment.”

It comes amid rumours the Russia establishment is closer than ever to launching a coup to oust Putin and save their own wealth.

Russia’s oligarchs and top officials have long formed the backbone of Putin’s rule, providing control over the economy, security forces, and state media.



But since war broke out, many of Russia’s wealthiest figures have become trapped in the state by Western sanctions.

For the first time in generations, the interests of the ruling elite do not align with the dictator, insiders previously told The Sun.

Putin is also “lonely” in terms of foreign support.

Corn said: “The example of Iran shows again he has limited ability to support his allies.



“His number one partner now is China – which views Russia as a lesser, not equal partner.”

Putin has tried to persuade the world he is close with the US President.

But Corn said: “If he goes too far against Trump, that could backfire on him quickly.

“He also has to understand that Trump is a one term president and the next US president may not be open to trying to engage Putin, leaving him more isolated.”

In recent weeks, Ukraine has intensified its strategic bombing campaign against Russia’s oil industry.



The attacks have inflicted significant damage on Moscow’s war economy.

It comes as Ukraine expands its defence cooperation with European partners, including agreements with the UK on drone supply and production.

In a chilling response, the Kremlin brazenly listed dozens of European locations they would target with Russian missiles.

Russia’s Ministry of Defence (MoD) said the alleged war supply hotspots are “increasingly drawing these countries into war with Russia”.

Former Russian president, turned Kremlin propaganda puppet, Dmitry Medvedev said Western leaders should take the threat “literally”.



With the UK’s relationship with America under strain, Britain must strengthen its alliances elsewhere.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Dr Deyermond said: “The UK needs to work with other countries inside and outside NATO to protect against the threats from Russia.

“Ukraine, with its unique expertise in fighting a major war against Russia, will be an important partner that alliance.”

News.title: China KNEW pilot deliberately crashed Boeing 737 into mountain at 350mph killing 132 for four years, US probe reveals
News.content:
CHINESE authorities have known for four years that a pilot crashed a Boeing 737 deliberately, killing all 132 on board, a US probe has revealed.

China Eastern Airlines Flight 5735 smashed into a mountain at 350mph in Guangxi after the captain intentionally brought down the aircraft, newly surfaced data reveals.





The tragic collision on March 21, 2022, took place after one of the three airmen on board shut down both engines and turned off auto-pilot, according to the US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB).

Bombshell flight recordings show two of the pilots wrestling for control of the plane, before one of them eventually manages to push the jet into a nosedive.

The aircraft was travelling at close to the speed of sound when it crashed.

Beijing has failed to release an official report on the aviation catastrophe – despite mounting outrage from victims’ families and the public.



Suppressive Chinese authorities claimed last year that releasing information related to the disaster could “endanger national security and social stability”.

The recorders on Flight 5735 have now been decoded by the NTSB, who revealed their contents on Thursday.



The report said: “It was found that while cruising at 29,000ft, the fuel switches on both engines moved from the run position to the cut-off position.”

It added: “Engine speeds decreased after the fuel switch movement.”

Control input and jet movement graphs show that one of the pilot’s tried to push the aircraft into a steep nosedive while the other tried to stop it.



The two airmen steered fiercely in opposite directions as they fought to gain control over the packed aircraft.

Voice recordings also captured the exchange taking place between the two pilots in the moments before their deaths.

But the NTSB did not reveal what exactly was said – adding that it had sent a transcript to Beijing.



Horror footage taken from the ground showed the huge jet plummeting vertically.

No radio calls or emergency radar codes were made by the crew.

An alleged cover-up by Chinese authorities has included local media reports that all systems were functioning normally in the moments leading up to the tragedy.

A US investigator told The Wall Street Journal two months after the crash that the plane “did what it was told to do by someone in the cockpit”.

Iron-fisted Chinese authorities censored the WSJ report from social media – taking down screenshots and covering up allegations of a murder-suicide by the pilot.



There were three pilots on the flight deck at the time.

Captain Yang Hongda, 32, Zhang Zhengping, the 59-year-old first officer, and Ni Gongtao, a 27-year-old second officer in training.

Zhang, one of the airline’s most experienced pilots, had recently been demoted from his captain’s rank in early 2022.

Speculation of an alleged murder-suicide have centred on him.

Intentionally crashing has proved to be one of the leading causes of plane disasters in recent years, reports say.



It was the second most common cause of plane deaths from 2011 to 2020, Bloomberg reported.

It comes after the Air India Flight 171 catastrophe which killed 260 people after taking off from Ahmedabad en route to London last year.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A report is set to be released next month, after previous experts claimed the crash was caused by deliberate pilot action.

Indian authorities have rejected claims that a pilot murder-suicide caused the crash.

News.title: Husband of Miss Switzerland finalist on trial over murder of wife who ‘was decapitated and had body parts blended’
News.content:
DEPRAVED KILLING Husband of Miss Switzerland finalist on trial over murder of wife who ‘was decapitated and had body parts blended’

THE husband of a Miss Switzerland finalist has gone on trial today over the gruesome death of his wife.

Marc Rieben, 42, allegedly flew into a rage before murdering Kristina Joksimovic – as a shocking autopsy revealed he dismembered her body and “pureed” parts of it in a blender.





Today, as the trial opens at Basel-Landschaft Criminal Court in Muttenz, the public are excluded from the courthouse, which has been ringed by police and security.

Rieben is charged with murdering Kristina and desecration of the dead. He faces life in prison if found guilty.

According to Blick, the defendant was led into court wearing handcuffs after being held in isolation in prison since his arrest.

According to the indictment, violence erupted during an argument over the couple’s separation on February 13, 2024.



Over lunch, the pair discussed splitting up – but Rieben allegedly refused to accept the divorce, demanded full custody of their children and denied financial support.

What followed, prosecutors say, was a chilling and calculated descent into brutality.

During the altercation, Rieben – the son of a successful lawyer – allegedly grabbed Kristina by the throat and slammed her against a wall.

He then used a “ribbon-like object” to strangle her before embarking on a campaign of mutilation that investigators say was both deliberate and methodical.



An autopsy revealed revealed a catalogue of injuries – blunt force trauma, cuts to her face, bruising across her body and hair torn from her scalp.

After killing her, Rieben dismembered her body using a jigsaw, a knife and garden shears.

Investigators say he “carefully removed” her womb – the only organ taken – in what experts described as a “deliberate mutilation or ritualised degradation of the body.”



Some parts were placed into an industrial blender, while others were dissolved in chemicals.

In a chilling detail, investigators found he had been playing YouTube videos on his phone as he carried out the dismemberment.

The family home’s basement laundry room – described as an “isolated bunker with thick concrete walls” – became the scene of unimaginable horror.

There, police later discovered “a large number” of skin flaps, “some with attacked muscles,” alongside fragments of bone and tissue.

The gruesome crime was uncovered not by police, but by Kristina’s own father.



When she failed to collect her daughters from kindergarten, her parents became alarmed.

Her father went to her house, where Rieben reportedly claimed he had no idea where she was.

For hours, he reportedly behaved as though nothing was wrong as he cooked dinner, put the children to bed and spoke calmly to his father-in-law.



“Rieben kept insisting he didn’t know where Kristina was and claimed she would just leave sometimes,” a friend said.

As Rieben spoke to Kristina’s mother on the phone, her father searched the house.

In the basement, he spotted a black bin bag with strands of blonde hair protruding.

“When he opened the black bin bag, he saw her cut off head with the hair still attached,” the friend said.

He ran outside screaming, begging a passerby to call police, before returning to confront his son-in-law.



Kristina was a glamorous former Miss Switzerland finalst and catwalk coach. Her social media showed smiling family photos with their two young daughters.

Weeks before her death, images showed a romantic “couple’s getaway” with Rieben at Lake Lucerne.

The couple, who married in 2017, lived in an upscale semi-detached home in Binningen, near Basel – a quiet, affluent neighbourhood where Rieben was seen as a model husband.

Neighbours described Rieben as a “devoted father”.

Former Miss Switzerland Nadine Vinzens said: “She always made a happy impression on me. I would never have thought that her husband would do something like that.”



Another friend added: “To me, they seemed like the perfect family.”

Following his arrest, Rieben reportedly showed no emotion.

Through his lawyers, he has confessed, but said he acted in self-defence because Kristina attacked him.

He alleged that moments before her death, Kristina “suddenly attacked him with a knife” after what he described as a “positive” conversation.

He said he carried out the mutilation “in a panic”.



An expert rejected his self-defence claim, pointing out that victims of genuine life-threatening attacks typically contact police immediately – not embark on a “prompt, purposeful, and methodically executed” effort to destroy evidence.

His actions, the expert said, only make sense if he was trying to “eliminate as many traces as possible, including the body, in order to conceal what actually happened”.

Prosecutors say Rieben had a history of violence, including previously choking his wife – evidence supported by earlier photographs – and assaulting a former partner.

According to the indictment, the killing was carried out deliberately, driven by “a selfish attitude and mindset characterised by a need for control, hurt feelings, revenge, and intense rage”.

Rieben has been in custody since his arrest.



Media are following the trial via video link, with only judges, prosecutors, defence lawyers, defendants and family allowed in the courtroom.

Because of strict Swiss privacy laws, Rieben is being referred to in local media as Thomas L, while Kristina – a former Miss Switzerland finalist – is Ivana L.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Rieben denies the charges against him.

The trial is expected to last five and a half days.

News.title: Man, 19, arrested after ‘series’ of sexual assaults in Sainsbury’s supermarket
News.content:
SUPERMARKET HORROR Man, 19, arrested after ‘series’ of sexual assaults in Sainsbury’s supermarket

COPS have arrested a teenager after a “series” of alleged sexual assaults at a Sainsbury’s.

Sussex Police said multiple women reported incidents taking place on the escalator leaving the superstore in Rustington, West Sussex.



The force confirmed that a 19-year-old man has been arrested for sexual assault by touching.



Cops are appealing for witnesses and have urged anyone with information to come forward immediately.

The force thanked the co-operation of Sainsbury’s security which helped lead to the arrest.

A spokesman for Sussex Police said: “Our enquiries, with the co-operation of Sainsbury’s security, have led to a 19-year-old man from Littlehampton being arrested for sexual assault by touching.

“Any witnesses and victims are encouraged to contact police on 101, quoting serial 1021 of 02/05.”

News.title: How undercover chef spent a decade infiltrating North Korea to expose arms deal & Kim’s bid to dodge sanctions
News.content:
DEEP undercover in the world’s most secretive regime, a retired Danish chef turned spy spent ten gruelling years exposing North Korea’s crime-ridden engine.

Ulrich Larsen, known as “the Mole”, rubbed shoulders with the powerful foreign representatives and figures in the Hermit Kingdom – eventually getting his hands on a weapons list that resembled a “pizza menu”.





He told The Sun the inside story of how he found the smoking gun that proves how organised crime keeps Kim Jong-Un’s evil regime afloat.

Ulrich’s journey to Pyongyang all started with an inflamed pancreas.

The illness became chronic, and forced an early retirement from a career as a successful Copenhagen chef.

During one of many long stints in hospital, the Dane stumbled across a documentary called The Red Chapel, by storied filmmaker Mads Brugger.

The 88-minute exposé follows two comedians disguised as a vaudeville act, who methodically lay bare North Korea’s iron-fisted oppression.

The Hermit Kingdom has long been the subject of sweeping UN sanctions – its punishment for pursuing an aggressive nuclear weapons programme and threatening an apocalypse on the West.

Within its borders, millions are subjected to human rights violations beyond comprehension and dystopian bloodhounds work tirelessly to sniff out dissenters.

As Supreme Dictator Kim lines his pockets and triple XL stomach, the majority of his people starve on stale rice.



But in order to rake in the much-needed cash to fund his lavish diet and nuclear hobbies, Kim and his cronies have been forced to hatch plots to traffic military-grade weapons and class A drugs.

Paranoid state police keep an eagle eye over every square inch of the regime, but for all their guile, were outfoxed by a daring Danish man with a handheld camera.

Brugger’s documentary flicked a switch in Ulrich, who recalled childhood trips behind the Iron Curtain to the communist dictatorship of its day, East Germany.

Inspired by Brugger’s work, Ulrich wanted to help expose the reality of life in North Korea and wormed his way into Denmark’s Korean Friendship Association – a fanatical society of North Korea supporters.



He told The Sun: “I found a little old Danish association supporting North Korea, all everyday people aged 60 and over, who were having a meeting in Copenhagen.

“I started creating a lie for the Danish chairman, writing that when I was a kid I experienced East Germany and it was the most fantastic place on Earth, because everybody had a job.”

Ulrich’s bait worked, and Korean Friendship Association President and diehard communist Anders Kristensen welcomed him in with open arms.

The next step would be to team up with filmmaker Brugger, who was by this point a recognised opponent of the regime, to create a trap and gain access to North Korea.



Ulrich said: “I reached out to Brugger on Facebook but did not expect an answer. He said later that I was his lottery ticket back to North Korea.”

What followed was a carefully crafted infiltration, pinned on a stroke of genius that paved the way for their documentary – The Mole: Undercover in North Korea.

To maintain his cover and a reason to film, Ulrich introduced himself as an propagandist to the Korean Friendship Association.

He pitched the idea of producing small clips to show the “true story” of the Hermit Kingdom.

Ulrich said: “The Korean Friendship Association are just a bunch of useless idiots for the regime.”



Ulrich was promoted to board member, which eventually gave him access to North Korea itself.

The Danish Korean Friendship Association, like other branches around the world, were invited to Pyongyang for recognition.

Ulrich was personally awarded a friendship medal for his loyalty and perceived propaganda efforts.



In turn, he was allowed to record far more freely than most visitors – and continued building credibility over repeated trips, embedding himself deeper into the secretive regime.

His connections eventually led him to Alejandro Cao de Benos – a Spanish aristocrat and infamous Kim family bootlicker.

As the head of central Korean Friendship Association and known as the “Gatekeeper of North Korea”, Cao de Benos worked for the regime soliciting donations to fund the sanction-dodging schemes.

“In North Korea, he was the most powerful Western man, no doubt about it,” Ulrich said.

Cao de Benos was acquiring donations to fund his authoritarian overlords and bolster his own dictatorial status.



After three years building trust with Cao de Benos, Ulrich needed another character to act as a businessman with money to invest in North Korea.

They brought in Jim Latrache-Qvortrup – a convicted drug dealer coming off the back of an eight-year prison stint – to pose as “Mr James”, a wealthy businessman reminiscent of a suave Bond villain.

The aim was to set up a meeting between Cao de Benos and Mr James in a bid to expose North Korea’s illegal arms trade.

Ulrich served as the mediator at the introduction between Alejandro and Mr James at a plush Oslo hotel suite, which was secretly recorded.

“After only five minutes, [Alejandro] started talking about drugs, weapons, regular pharmaceuticals and missiles”, Ulrich recalled.



“We were sitting in front of a man who represents the North Korean regime.

“He’s been awarded several medals. He met the leaders. At that point, we didn’t know if he was also just bragging to maybe gain 10,000 Euros in the pocket.”

Ulrich said they took the “big and dangerous step” of going from working with “stupid” people supporting North Korea to “people doing criminal activities with North Korea”.



Before returning to the Hermit Kingdom to hammer out a staged arms deal, the spy was flown out to Washington to receive special security training from a former CIA agent called “Max”.

Ulrich said: “He made it quite clear to me. If you get found out, you die.”

After a nerve-racking flight, Ulrich and Mr James were greeted with VIP treatment in Pyongyang from friends of Cao de Benos.

Maintaining their deep cover, they were gearing up for a secret meeting that would expose the regime’s dodgy deals.

The pair were driven to the outskirts of Pyongyang – an area no foreigner would be welcome on one of the regime’s carefully choreographed tours.



They were led into a crumbling building and directed towards a stairwell.

Ulrich said: “They asked us to go down to a basement in the building.

“From those roughly 50 steps from the car to the door, I was expecting to be killed, but I couldn’t show any fear.

“I was walking in front, down to the basement, and it was getting darker and darker. I thought, ‘in a second, I’m going to hear this sound from the gun, and then lights out’.”

Miraculously, after pushing through a heavy black leather door, Ulrich was greeted by an absurd sight.



He said: “There were lights like the ones you see at a disco, and I thought – my God, they’re gonna do some psychological terror on us and then they’re gonna kill us.

“There was this huge table filled with every kind of food you could expect in the Western world. The people outside the door have never seen this kind of stuff before. There were beers, Coca-Cola, everything.”

Later, North Korean arms and “pharmaceutical” chiefs stopped by to talk business.



As they discussed trafficking plots over household snacks, Ulrich and Mr James were greeted by a weapons list that resembled a “pizza menu”.

The meeting took an even stranger turn when an arms boss called a pause and broke into an impromptu karaoke performance.

Ulrich said: “In the middle of everything, he just walks to a laptop, takes a microphone in his hand, and starts singing.

“We were talking about buying an island in Africa to build a factory… and now I’m singing North Korean karaoke.

“Then they gave me the microphone and said, ‘your turn, Mr Larsen’. And the music starts and I was expecting Let It Be or Hey Jude, but they put on Celine Dion’s My Heart Will Go On from Titanic.



“I’m a bad singer, but not to lose face, I start improvising a Danish children’s song I would sing for my daughters when they were small, and doing funny things with my arms and legs.

“Then I sat down and emptied a bottle of beer to relax, when a North Korean who’s been standing behind me puts his hands on my shoulders.

“I thought, ‘s*** he’s gonna kill me’, but he said, ‘I can feel that song came directly from you heart. I can feel in your heart that you love our dear leader’.

“It was because it reminds me of my children, but for them, everything is about the three Kims.”

Once the meeting finished, Ulrich, Mr James and their North Korean handlers got to work.



After earmarking Namibia as a potential host to build a weapons factory, diplomatic ties were severed and attention turned to Uganda.

Ulrich said: “We found an island for sale in Lake Victoria and we went there to see it. We were told there were maybe 300 or 400 people living there who could be moved.

“So we hired a helicopter to take a flyover, and so the North Koreans could see it from above. From above, there were probably more like 3,000 4,000 people in total on the island.”



Local intermediaries appeared unfazed at the prospect of booting their people out.

They said that once $5million (£3.7m) was transferred, the islanders would be removed.

To maintain the cover story, Ulrich and his team were forced to play along, promising things they could not deliver.

Efforts were being made to solve the challenge of moving building materials and payments without breaching international sanctions.

This led to the introduction of a Jordanian businessman who claimed to have the necessary connections.



He told Ulrich and Mr James that he could arrange oil shipments from Russia and move them using ghost tankers that could not be traced.

The ships would sail in areas without satellite coverage, change identity, or transfer cargo at sea so it could not be tracked.

Instead of paying money, North Korea would send workers and equipment to skirt around the sanctions.

A meeting was arranged in Copenhagen to outline the iron out the final details of the deal.

“We met at the most exclusive hotel in Denmark for everything to be signed and we got a whole menu of weapons with the manuals,” Ulrich said.



At this point, the filmmakers were preparing to bring the scheme to an abrupt end.

They would withdraw the fictional investor and cause the deal to collapse before any real transaction could take place.

Ulrich said: “Mr James disappeared, and was told to become a ghost.”

He was surprised when Cao de Benos appeared unfazed and was willing to move the plan along.

But Brugger and Ulrich decided it was time to make the grand reveal in a carefully orchestrated video call.



He said: “I just start telling him about who I am and what I did. And then after about 20 seconds, Mads sat next to me and told him we got everything on tape.

“He simply switched [the video call] off. And that’s the last I heard from him.”

Far from fearing for his life, it has returned to relative normality, Ulrich said.

Keen to share his story, he said: “I don’t hate North Korea. I don’t hate North Korean citizens. I hate the people running the country.”

Reflective on what he was able to achieve, Ulrich said: “I’m proud of all the nice words I had, but I feel a bit scared because the CIA or MI5, MI6 or FBI are not able to do what I did.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I think the reason they couldn’t do it is because they are acting like agents, where I was 95 per cent myself and the last 5 per cent was the mole.”

But Ulrich ultimately achieved what he set out to do, saying: “It was my fault that there will be even more sanctions on North Korea after the release of The Mole.”

News.title: Nigel Farage's chilling detention centres plan as Reform 'sinks to new low'
News.content:
Nigel Farage's chilling detention centres plan as Reform 'sinks to new low'

Home Affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf faced fury after announcing plans to lock up tens of thousands of migrants in detention facilities in locations controlled by parties other than Reform

View 3 Images Nigel Farage’s Reform UK is facing a backlash after unveiling “abhorrent” migration plans (Image: Thomas Krych/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Nigel Farage’s Reform UK is facing a backlash after unveiling “abhorrent” plans to introduce huge detention centres in areas that don’t vote for their party.

‌



Home Affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf faced fury after announcing plans to lock up tens of thousands of migrants at a time in locations controlled by parties other than Reform. He said no constituencies with a Reform MP or a Reform-controlled council would have a detention facility.

‌



He vowed to prioritise areas where the Green Party is in power to carry out its mass deportation plans as it claimed the party is in favour of "open borders".

‌



Labour's chair Anna Turley branded the plans "grotesque" and said punishing places where people don't vote for Reform is a "betrayal of basic democratic principles". The Greens said the proposals were "abhorrent", and a former senior Tory minister said the proposals would likely be “an abuse of ministerial power for political purposes”.

Nigel Farage's campaign descends into racism row after Reform candidate turns on key member READ MORE :

View 3 Images Home Affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf faced fury after announcing the plans (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Critics also raised concerns that choosing areas because of political motivations could mean sites are unsuitable. Targeting Green areas could mean opening detention centres in urban or densely populated cities, where the Green Party is most popular. Businessman Mr Yusuf posted a video promoting the plans filmed in Brighton, which he said could be an area Reform considers.

‌



Reform's draconian plans, unveiled on Sunday night, come as voters head to the polls in local elections across parts of England and in the devolved administrations of Scotland and Wales. Insurgent parties like Reform and the Greens are expected to make huge gains, with Labour expected to suffer devastating losses.

In a furious statement on Monday morning, Labour's Ms Turley said: “This grotesque policy reveals Reform’s contempt for all voters - including their own. Threatening to punish places where people don’t vote your way is a betrayal of basic democratic principles. Nigel Farage has sunk to a new low: he is clearly more interested in stoking division and anger than in serving the whole country.

“Labour has always been clear that we need a fair, controlled asylum system that works in Britain’s national interest – and that’s what we’re delivering. We’ve taken decisive action to bear down on small boat crossings and restore control of our borders. We're going further and closing asylum hotels around the country - regardless of what party local people voted for.

‌



“Nigel Farage doesn’t care about fixing the system – he just wants to drive a toxic wedge between our communities."

View 3 Images Nigel Farage's party is expected to make huge gains at the local elections (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Responding to the plans on social media, Labour peer George Foulkes said: “An astonishing threat from an unelected Reform apparatchik.”

‌



And a Green Party spokeswoman said the plans were a "disgusting idea", adding: “Reform keep making abhorrent announcements in attempts to distract voters from the fact they want to privatise our NHS, roll back workers rights and hand out tax breaks to their billionaire backers."

Former senior Tory MP Simon Clarke, who served as Chief Secretary to the Treasury, said: "We need to stop illegal immigration, but this is abhorrent from Reform. Zia is proposing the siting of detention centres expressly as a form of political punishment for people and places that don’t vote Reform - not just Green, but presumably Conservative, Liberal and Labour too. (And what about Reform voters in those constituencies?) It would almost certainly be deemed an abuse of ministerial power for political purposes."

He added that choosing the location for detention centres for political purposes might mean the sites are not “in any way suitable for the proposed centres, or near the other infrastructure required”.

Article continues below

Announcing the policy, Mr Yusuf said: "A Reform government will not put any migrant detention facilities in any constituency with a Reform MP. Nor will we put them where Reform controls the council. And of the remaining areas, we will prioritise Green controlled parliamentary constituencies and Green controlled councils to locate the detention centres.

"Put simply, if you vote in a Reform council or Reform MP, we guarantee you won’t have a detention centre near you. If you vote Green, there’s a good chance you will. This is an important exercise in democratic consent, not just for our mass deportation policy, but for where the detention centres are placed. Given Zack Polanski openly advocates for open borders, I look forward to their warm embrace of this policy."

News.title: Iran war live: US frigate 'hit by missiles in Hormuz' after Trump vow to free ships
News.content:
A US Navy frigate sailed through the Strait of Hormuz today 'in violation of traffic and shipping security' before it was attacked with missiles, Iran says

Two Iranian missiles have struck a US Navy frigate after it "ignored a warning" from Iran and sailed through the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media has claimed.

The frigate is said to have passed into the global shipping route today "in violation of traffic and shipping security" near Jask. It was targeted by a missile attack after ignoring a warning from Iran's Navy and then forced to retreat and flee the area, reports the Fars news agency.

Details on the extent of damage and possible casualties have not yet been confirmed. The reported attack comes after Donald Trump said that "for the good of Iran, the Middle East, and the United States" American forces would begin to escort ships belonging to countries "that have absolutely nothing to do with the war" from the Strait of Hormuz.

The President did not specify exactly which countries he means.

News.title: All the supermarket items to buy NOW as food prices set to rise by 50% due to Iran war
News.content:
All the supermarket items to buy NOW as food prices set to rise by 50% due to Iran war

The war in the Middle East is putting pressure on supply chains by pushing up fuel and energy costs - and some examples of higher prices have already been highlighted

View 3 Images Our shopping bills seem to go up every day (Image: Getty Images)

UK households have been warned that food prices are likely to keep rising - with everyday essentials such as oil and pasta having already taken some of the worst hits.

‌



New research from the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU) think tank shows food prices are on track to be 50% higher by November compared to levels at the start of the cost of living crisis in mid-2021.

‌



The “grim milestone” is due to a combination of extreme weather driven by climate change, global supply disruptions, and volatile oil and gas markets.

‌



The war in the Middle East is putting pressure on supply chains by pushing up fuel and energy costs. Increased energy and fuel costs can impact several factors of food production, including transportation and the running of machinery .These extra costs are typically passed down to consumers.

View 3 Images The Strait of Hormuz has been blocked for several weeks now (Image: Getty Images)

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has also caused disruption of fertiliser supplies, which are used to grow fruit and vegetables. About a third of the world's fertilisers normally pass through the Strait, according to the United Nations.

‌



According to the analysis, the cost of staples including pasta, frozen vegetables, chocolate, eggs and beef are already up between 50% and 64%. Olive oil is also up 113% having first endured big increases in price during the cost of living crisis.

Other climate-impacted foods that are putting pressure on food inflation include butter, milk and coffee, with these foods rising over four times faster than other products.

Latest inflation figures from Worldpanel by Numerator show grocery prices are currently 3.8% higher than a year ago, with households warned that the Middle East conflict has “not yet” filtered through to supermarket shelves.

‌



The Food and Drink Federation (FDF), which represents 12,000 food and drink manufacturers, has warned food inflation could reach 9% by the end of 2026. Separately, businesses have told the Bank of England that UK food inflation could reach 7%.

View 3 Images Petrol prices have gone up massively (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

Chris Jaccarini, food and farming analyst at the ECIU, said: “Trump’s war in the Middle East is set to drive shopping bills higher as oil and gas prices spike.

‌



“Scientists are predicting 2027 to be the hottest year on record with climate change combining with the El Nino effect kicking off this year. Three of England’s worst harvests on record have been in the past five years.

“Unless we get to net zero emissions to stop climate change and bring balance to the system, food prices will spiral ever further, but net zero also means burning less oil and gas, so insulating our food system from the kind of price spikes we’ve been seeing since Russian invaded Ukraine.”

Anna Taylor, executive director of the Food Foundation, said: “Food prices rising this high and this fast leaves families on the lowest incomes with nowhere left to cut except the food on their plate.

‌



“When that happens, people skip meals, children go hungry, and diet-related illness rises – taking parents out of work and piling pressure on an NHS that can least afford it.

“This conflict is the latest shock in a series, and there will be more. The question for Government isn’t just how to respond to this crisis – it’s whether we’re finally going to build a food system resilient enough to withstand the next one.”

We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

‌



Which items to buy now?

While there is no need to panic buy, shoppers may want to consider stocking up on certain items now in case they do keep rising in price.

We've looked at some examples of some food that has already gone up in price and worked out how much more it could cost if prices rise by another 50% based on the ECIU report.

This isn't to say prices for these specific items will rise by this much, but is more to demonstrate a worst-case scenario increase, based on average prices now.

‌



If prices were to rise by 50% then it could see shoppers spend an extra £16 on these items alone. We've analysed the average price across different supermarkets, as opposed to the cheapest possible.

You should only buy what you will definitely use, and things that have a long expiry life or can be frozen, to avoid food waste.

Data from Waste and Resources Action Programme (Wrap) shows the average household of four spends a whopping £1,000 each year on good food that goes in the bin and could have been eaten.

‌



Pasta

The average price of a 500g bag of supermarket own brand pasta is around 60p. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price of pasta could hit 90p.

Frozen vegetables

The average price of a 1kg bag of supermarket own brand mixed frozen vegetables is about 99p. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price would be £1.49.

Chocolate

The average price of a 200g bar of supermarket own brand chocolate is around £2.10. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price would be £3.15.

‌



Eggs

The average price of a box of six supermarket own brand medium eggs is about £1.70. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price would be £2.55.

Beef

The average price of supermarket own brand beef is around £15 per kg. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price would be £22.50.

Olive oil

The average price of 1L of supermarket own brand beef olive oil is about £6.15. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price would be £9.20.

‌



Butter

The average price of a 250g block of supermarket own brand butter is around £1.99. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price would be £2.98.

Milk

The average price of a four pints of supermarket own brand milk is £1.65. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price would be £2.46.

Coffee

The average price of a 200g jar of supermarket own brand coffee is £2.50. If this was to rise by 50% then it would mean the average price would be £3.75.

News.title: Paul McCartney and Mick Jagger planned Rolling Beatles supergroup despite 'arch rivalry'
News.content:
Paul McCartney and Mick Jagger planned Rolling Beatles supergroup despite 'arch rivalry'

The Rolling Stones and The Beatles were rivals, but a new book, The World’s Greatest Rock n Roll Band reveals there was another partnership brewing between Jagger and McCartney

View 6 Images Paul McCartney (L) and Mick Jagger attend the Metropolitan Museum of Art's 2011 Costume Institute Gala featuring the opening of the exhibit Alexander McQueen : Savage Beauty (Image: Penske Media via Getty Images)

Music legend portrays The Rolling Stones and The Beatles as arch rivals. Beatlemania came first, but Lennon and McCartney’s songwriting genius inspired Jagger and Richards to follow suit - penning their first global smash, (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction in 1965, which topped the charts in the UK and the US. Now a new book, The World’s Greatest Rock n Roll Band, by music journalist Bob Spitz, reveals there was another partnership brewing between Jagger and McCartney.

‌



The original ‘frenemies,’ the canny businessmen came close to forming a ‘Rolling Beatles’-style supergroup, with plans to dominate the British music industry. Spitz says: "Mick and Paul wanted to start their own studios and record label. They were very close to doing that. Paul and Mick were the business minds of their bands.”

‌



After manager Andrew Oldham resigned in 1967, The Stones never had another manager - effectively leaving it to Mick, says Spitz. He continues: "Mick and Paul had got together and sensed they had a stranglehold on the scene, so why not have a business stranglehold? They wanted headquarters, one company, one label, but John [Lennon] and George [Harrison] were not going for it."

‌



View 6 Images All aboard the "love" train...Beatle Paul McCartney, wearing an Indian-style jacket, and Mick Jagger (left) of the Rolling Stones, walk toward train en route to a love pilgrimage to Bangor. (Image: Bettmann Archive)

McCartney even devised a plan to create a joint Beatles/Stones HQ at a disused brewery in Camden, north London. Spitz says: "Mick went to see it and thought it was great. They had investment money put aside. Paul even wanted a heliport, so they could fly bands in and out. I think Paul was fantasising quite a bit and whatever Mick is, he is not a fantasist. He is a straight head cold blooded businessman. That just did not make sense to him. If the Beatles and Stones had got together, who knows what would have happened."

The plans never came to fruition. But Jagger and RIchards’ songwriting prowess helped The Stones sell more than 250 million albums worldwide and gross $2.9billion at the box office from touring. Sadly, their perfect harmonies did not play-out off stage. Jagger lost tolerance with Richards’ ongoing drug abuse. He, in turn, gave short thrift to Jagger’s solo ambitions. Spitz says: "Mick and Keith have renewed their vows so many times it is ridiculous.”

‌



Saved by never being in competition, he explains: "Mick was the peacock and Keith was the master of riffs. They were just able to not get in each other's face except in the mid 90s when they almost teetered on divorce. It was a love story from the very beginning."

View 6 Images Ronnie Wood and Mick Jagger performing live on stage (Image: Redferns)

Richards’ drug use spiralled out of control on the road after releasing their 1976 Black and Blue album. Kicking off the tour in Frankfurt, West Germany, Spitz recalls a strung out Keith winding up on his bottom on stage and continuing to play. He adds: "In Münster, in the midst of Fool to Cry, he was so wasted that he fell asleep on stage. He nursed an appetite for heroin and cocaine. In restaurants, he'd snort cocaine right off a dinner plate while openmouthed maître d's and waiters stood by.”

‌



But when he fell asleep at the wheel of his Bentley, driving back to London from the Midlands in a storm in 1976, he and his passengers were lucky to escape alive. Spitz says: “Hitting 100 mph, he nodded off and sent his Bentley careening off the M1 motorway and through a barrier, coming to rest in a farmer's field.

"The passengers - his son, Marlon, Freddie Sessler (brother of London restaurateur Siegi Sessler) and two women - miraculously escaped unhurt. Keith ditched his stash under a bush. But three policemen were on the scene in no time, one of whom noticed a coke spoon attached to a silver necklace on the floor of the battered car. That precipitated a strip search at the police station, where a blotter of LSD was found in the pocket of Keith's jacket. His explanation was feeble, ‘it could belong to anyone’. He was promptly arrested."

View 6 Images The Rolling Stones, in a vintage car 1964. From left to right Brian Jones, Mick Jagger, Bill Wyman, Charlie Watts and Keith Richards (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The crash resulted in drugs charges and a £750. Spitz says: "Keith was seriously f*cked up, taking industrial quantities of drugs. Physically, he was wasted; his frame was emaciated, his eyes sunken, his teeth blackened and rotting. Sure, some of this came with the territory for a rock'n roller, but he was courting disaster.”

Likewise, Ronnie Wood's drug battles over the years are legendary. He joined The Stones in 1975, replacing Mick Taylor, who could no longer hack the lifestyle.Former Rolling Stones Records president Marshall Chess, 84, recalls: "In my apartment in New York, I had a cocaine-sniffing Art Deco table with a black glass top. Freddie Sessler [late restaurateur] would come by with one of his brown-glass bottles, dump out a massive amount of cocaine, and Ronnie and I hit that table like Peter Rabbit running."

But at the dawn of the Eighties, Jagger lost patience and threatened to let Wood go. Spitz says: "When the Stones decided to go back on the road in the fall of 1981, they floated the idea that it might be better if Woody didn't accompany them. Keith, of course, went to bat for him. Keith knew the importance of the band as a safety net when you were in the grip of drugs. Woody assured him he'd be cool, he'd stay off the pipe."

‌



View 6 Images Guitarist Keith Richards (R) and vocalist Mick Jagger of rock & roll group The Rolling Stones on the set of music programme Ready Steady Go! in London, circa 1964 (Image: TV Times/Future Publishing via Getty Images)

Spitz recalls things reaching a head on a US tour, when Richards caught Wood taking drugs on the sly. It was at a gig where they were supported by then unknown artist Prince. Spitz continues: “Woody, who held his own under the lights, was hitting the pipe on the sly. Keith took it personally. He decked Ronnie before a San Francisco gig.”

When the European leg of the tour started in May 1982, Mick wanted to sack Wood. He says: "He'd even made advances to George Thorogood, who played a wicked blues guitar, about taking over for Woody. When it was clear Ronnie would accompany the band to Europe, Mick insisted he stay elsewhere, apart from the band, and put him on a weekly allowance to curb his access to drugs."

‌



Today, all three surviving Stones are squeaky clean, with Wood, now 78, celebrating 16 years sober as well as Richards, who stopped drinking in 2018 and ditched fags in 2020. Meanwhile, Mick - who had heart valve replacement surgery in 2019 following a scare - trains five to six days a week, focusing on stamina, cardio and flexibility, often supplemented by ballet and yoga. And they are preparing to release their 25th studio album, Foreign Tongues - which features Paul McCartney.

View 6 Images Mick Jagger and John Lennon attend Second Annual American Film Institute Lifetime Achievement Awards Honoring James Cagney on March 13, 1974 at the Century Plaza Hotel in Century City, California (Image: Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

Of his book, Spitz says: "At its heart, the story is about two boys, Mick and Keith, and their unique, fraught, alchemical bond, often tested, never sundered. The Glimmer Twins and the bandmates, like Charlie Watts, who found their groove in relation to this double star, made the trip intact, while those who struggled, like Brian Jones and Mick Taylor, were chewed up and spit out.

Article continues below

"This is a story with many dark corners. But whether Jagger and Richards sold their souls to the devil at the crossroads for blues greatness, or just squeezed their heroes for every drop of inspiration, in the end their connection to their music and to each other put them in a category of one, where they very much remain."

News.title: Twisted 'Scissor Sister' who chopped up mum's lover while 'out of it' on booze and drugs freed
News.content:
Twisted 'Scissor Sister' who chopped up mum's lover while 'out of it' on booze and drugs freed

Charlotte Mulhall, who brutally killed her mum's lover and dumped part of his body in a canal, is reportedly ready to make a 'new start' as she is given day release from prison

View 3 Images Charlotte Mulhall pictured in 2006

An evil 'Scissor Sister' who killed her mother's lover claimed she is a changed woman as she adapts to life outside of prison.

‌



Charlotte Mulhall, 44, was thrown behind bars for over 20 years for killing her mum Kathleen's Kenyan lover Farah Swaleh Noor, 38, in a horrific attack. She slit his throat with a blade after he made a pass at her sister Linda at their Dublin home in March 20, 2005, and they were drunk and high on ecstasy at the time.

‌



Mulhall is now being freed from jail on temporary release for a half or full day over the next few months, as she adapts to being free.

‌



View 3 Images The sisters brutally killed Farah Swaleh Noor, 38 (Image: RTE)

After the brutal attack, the sisters cut up the dead man's body in their bathroom with a bread knife before putting most of his remains in a suitcase. They dumped it in the Royal Canal, where it was found 10 days later, reports the Irish Mirror.

The 'Scissor Sisters' buried the man's head separately and reburied it in several spots after getting on a bus to Tallaght, south Dublin, but Noor's head has never been discovered. Mulhall, a mother-of-one, has kept out of trouble in Limerick Prison in recent years and is now being let out under licence from the Independent Probation Board.

‌



It is understood the killer has expressed deep remorse for the horrendous crime, according to the Irish Mirror. A prison source reportedly said: "Charlotte Mulhall has a lot of regrets and very few memories of what happened that night because she was so out of it on the booze and the drugs.

View 3 Images Charlotte Mulhall (r) and Linda Mulhall (l)

"She feels she has served her time and is grateful to get a second chance in life. She was incarcerated at a very young age and now has a real opportunity to put this shocking period of her life behind her, and make a new start."

‌



Her sister Linda Mulhall was released in 2018 after she served a 15-year sentence for manslaughter. The mother-of-four, a former heroin addict has kept out of trouble and has reportedly left the past behind her.

It is not known where the 44-year-old will live when she is let out later this summer and if she will return to Dublin. The mum-of-one would not be able to leave the UK without special permission, as she is being released on parole.

The prison insider added: "She will be released under the supervision of the Independent Parole Board on parole and they will be constantly checking up on her. She is being given all these day releases just like any other lifer coming to the end of their sentence so that she can adjust to life on the outside.

Article continues below

"She will probably hope to get a job and somewhere discreet to stay. She will be given help by the Probation Service to get back on her feet. The sentence she received is for life and if she breaks any of the terms of her release she will be immediately sent back to jail."

Mulhall has reportedly been given a release date with the source added they expect the killer to be out fully "by the end of the summer at the latest".

News.title: First picture of man charged with Peter Kay bomb hoax after court update
News.content:
First picture of man charged with Peter Kay bomb hoax after court update

The man charged following an alleged bomb hoax at Peter Kay's gig at the Utilita Arena, Birmingham, over the weekend, appeared in court today

View 4 Images Peter Kay's performance in Birmingham on Friday was evacuated and a man has since been charged (Image: BBC)

A man accused of a bomb hoax at a Peter Kay performance has appeared in court. On Friday, fans at the Utilita Arena, Birmingham, were evacuated less than an hour into the performance.

During an appearance today at Birmingham Magistrates' Court, Omar Majed, 19, was denied bail. Police reported that a "suspicious bag" had been found. While those in attendance were given no insight into why the performance had been cut short, a member of the production told the crowd that the show had to be pulled. Majed was charged with false communications relating to a bomb hoax, West Midlands Police confirmed.

Today, the teen of Washwood Heath, Birmingham, appeared before magistrates. In a statement on Saturday, the force said: "Following searches of the Utilita Arena last night no items of a suspicious nature were found. A 19-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of a bomb hoax offence and remains in custody this morning as our enquiries continue.

View 4 Images Omar Majed has been denied bail (Image: Alamy Live News.)

"We're grateful to everyone for their co-operation and understanding. As always our priority is the safety of the public." Later on Saturday evening, the force issued a new update, confirming that Majed had been charged.

They said: "A man has been charged in connection with the events which led to the evacuation of the Utilita Arena in Birmingham last night. Omar Majed, 19 has been charged with false communications relating to a bomb hoax.

"Majed, of Washwood Heath, Birmingham, has been remanded to appear before magistrates in Birmingham on 4 May. An evacuation of the arena was ordered yesterday evening after a report of a suspicious bag being left in the area.

View 4 Images Police swooped on the Utilita Arena in Birmingham on Friday (Image: Brad Jolly/ Mirror)

"Following searches, nothing suspicious was found and we are grateful to everyone for their co-operation and understanding. As always our priority is the safety of the public."

At the time, the arena, located in the City Centre, said: "Utilita Arena Birmingham has been evacuated as a precaution on the advice of West Midlands Police after a potential suspicious bag was found nearby.

"The safety and security of customers and our colleagues is our highest priority. We can confirm everyone was safely evacuated and that the venue is secure. Ticket holders will be contacted directly in due course."

View 4 Images Peter's performance was evacuated (Image: Steve Aspinall/PA Wire)

One audience member said the production crew whispered to Peter while he was on stage before the comic was rushed off. Steve Aspinall, who lives in Bideford, Devon said: "Two guys came on, one with a mic and headphones, one guy whispered to Peter Kay and then he and Peter Kay shot off down the side.

"To be honest, I thought it was part of the show at first. It was a strange atmosphere, eerie, just confused really (about) what was happening. But it was alright and everyone was calm and left quite quickly with no panic."

The evacuation was "calm and swift," according to another person in attendance, who explained that they'd overheard a bag had been left somewhere. "No messing, it was just all out," Miranda Richardson from Northampton said.

News.title: Alex Ligertwood dead: Former Santana singer dies days after last concert
News.content:
Alex Ligertwood dead: Former Santana singer dies days after last concert

Alexander 'Alex' Ligertwood, the former lead vocalist of Santana, has died at the age of 79, his wife has announced. The Scottish singer passed away peacefully in his sleep just two weeks after his last show

View 3 Images Ex-Santana lead singer Alex Ligertwood dies days after final concert (Image: Getty Images)

Former Santana frontman Alex Ligertwood has died aged 79, his wife has confirmed. The Scottish vocalist, famed as the lead singer for the Latin rock legends, died just a fortnight after his final performance.

‌



His wife, Shawn Brogan, shared the devastating news on Facebook, writing: "It's with great sadness and heartache to announce the passing of my sweet dear Alex Ligertwood, my husband of 25 years, we knew each other for 36 years.

‌



"Alex passed peacefully in his sleep with his doggy Bobo by his side yesterday. Alex was loved by so many. If you knew him, you loved him.

‌



3 View 3 Images Alex is believed to have died in his sleep last week (Image: Getty Images) 3 View 3 Images He performed his final concert just days ago (Image: WireImage for The Golf Digest Companies)

"He touched so many with his extraordinary voice. He was all heart and soul. His favorite thing in life was to make music, sing and to share his gift with us.

"He performed his last show just two weeks ago. I'm grateful for that. He did it his way, on his terms, till the end. I will always love you, my sweet Alex. Rest in peace. Soar and sing with the angels, my love. Please keep me & his family, Lynn & Stewart Locke, Alex, Jenny, Kali, Merci & Marilo in your prayers."

‌



Local media in Scotland reports that Alex died in his sleep on Thursday following several years of battling poor health. Ligertwood served as Santana's lead vocalist, the band established by guitarist Carlos Santana in 1966, intermittently from 1979 to 1994. He contributed to acclaimed albums including 1979's Marathon, 1981's Zebop! and Sacred Fire: Live In South America, which arrived in 1993.

His subsequent career saw collaborations with German tribute act The Magic Of Santana, alongside stints with Senate, Jeff Beck Group and the Average White Band. A statement posted on social media by The Magic Of Santana read: "We are so sad! We just heard about Alex J Ligertwood passed away!

"We had a great journey together with him and we learned so much about music, passion and friendship. He was one of the best singer on this planet and we will deeply miss him. Thank you Alex, for everything."

‌



Brian Auger said on X, formerly known as Twitter: "It is with an incredibly heavy heart that I must share the news that my dear friend and fellow traveller on The Oblivion Express, Alex Ligertwood, has passed away. The big band in the sky just got infinitely better with Alex’s arrival."

Meanwhile, Brian described Alex as "my dear friend and fellow traveller," in a Facebook post. He said: "To me, Alex aka 'Wee Eck' was simply the best singer to ever do it. In all my years of music, I never heard anyone who possessed that kind of range or that effortless, carefree ability to soar through a melody.

"He didn't just sing songs; he lived them. The world feels much quieter today without his voice, and I will miss my friend more than words can say.

Article continues below

"The big band in the sky just got infinitely better with Alex's arrival."

After last week's warmth, the first full week of May is set to see temperatures tumble across the UK.
